Equivalently, phi(n) is the number of invertible residue classes modulo n.
The product is over the distinct prime divisors of n. Multiplicativity plus the prime-power formula gives the product formula immediately.

items.text: Multiplicative does not mean phi(mn)=phi(m)phi(n) for arbitrary m and n; coprimality is required.
In the defining count, n itself is counted only when n=1.
The product formula uses each distinct prime once, regardless of its exponent in n.
For n>2, phi(n) is even; pairing a unit with its negative is one quick explanation.

items.text: Do not multiply by one factor for every repeated prime occurrence.
Do not confuse phi(n) with the number of prime factors of n.
Factoring n incorrectly propagates directly into the product formula.
